pl-l4d31c2-d1e112.summary: States that separation is twofold, bodily and sacramental.

pl-l4d31c2-d1e115.summary: Holds that spouses can separate bodily for fornication, or by common consent for religion, for a time or to the end.
claims: Bodily separation is allowed for fornication or religion.

pl-l4d31c2-d1e118.summary: Holds that, being lawful persons, they cannot be separated sacramentally while they live, the conjugal bond remaining even if they leave and cling to others.
claims: The marriage bond is indissoluble while they live.

pl-l4d31c2-d1e121.summary: Quotes Augustine: the rights of marriage once begun remain among the living, so that they are spouses to each other even when separated, rather than to those they joined.
claims: Separated spouses remain married to each other.

pl-l4d31c2-d1e131.summary: Adds Augustine: a conjugal bond remains among the living that neither separation nor union with another can remove, as the apostate soul, leaving Christ's marriage, does not lose the sacrament of faith received in baptism, which would otherwise be restored on return; it has it to its greater punishment.
claims: The marriage bond, like baptism, is not lost by apostasy.

pl-l4d31c2-d1e137.summary: Adds Augustine: for those who agreed to abstain perpetually, the bond is not broken but firmer, kept by affections of minds, not bodies.

pl-l4d31c2-d1e143.summary: Notes that the third good is called sacrament not because it is marriage itself but because it is the sign of the same sacred thing, the spiritual and inseparable union of Christ and the Church.
claims: The sacrament good signifies Christ's union with the Church.

pl-l4d31c2-d1e149.summary: Notes that some contract marriages these three goods do not accompany.

pl-l4d31c2-d1e152.summary: Explains that faith is lacking when one spouse unites with another; this good commends marriage when present but does not annul it when absent, since an adulteress is still a wife, else she would not be an adulteress; fault is committed, the sacrament not cancelled.
claims: Adultery lacks faith but does not annul marriage.

pl-l4d31c2-d1e157.summary: Explains that the good of offspring is not present in all spouses: some keep continence by mutual vow, others cannot generate for age or other causes; and not all with children have the good of offspring, which is not the child or the hope of heirs, but the desire for children to be formed in religion.
claims: The good of offspring is the desire for children raised in religion.

pl-l4d31c2-d1e164.summary: Concludes that many have children yet lack the good of offspring, and their marriage does not cease.

pl-l4d31c2-d1e167.summary: Holds that the sacrament inseparably accompanies the marriage of lawful persons, so that without it there seems no marriage, since the bond always remains while they live, even after divorce for fornication; where marriage is contracted between unlawful persons, this good is absent, since such unions can be dissolved.
claims: The sacrament good always accompanies lawful marriage.
Unions of unlawful persons can be dissolved.

pl-l4d31c2-d1e170.summary: Quotes Augustine on those who unite not for offspring but for incontinence, keeping faith: it may not absurdly be called marriage if they intend it until death and do not avoid offspring, either by refusing children or acting to prevent birth; otherwise not. One who takes a woman temporarily until finding a worthier wife is an adulterer in mind.
claims: Union for incontinence may be marriage if faith is kept and offspring not prevented.

pl-l4d31c2-d1e179.summary: Draws out that those who unite for intercourse alone are called spouses, provided they do not avoid generation by some evil means.
claims: Such unions are marriages if offspring is not prevented.

pl-l4d31c2.summary: Distinguishes bodily from sacramental separation: spouses may separate bodily for fornication or by mutual consent for religion, but cannot be separated sacramentally while they live, the bond remaining even if they cling to others, as the apostate keeps the sacrament of baptism. The third good is called sacrament because it signifies the inseparable union of Christ and the Church. Some marriages lack the goods: adultery lacks faith but does not annul marriage; many lack the good of offspring, which means the desire for children to be raised religiously, yet remain married; but the sacrament always accompanies marriage between lawful persons. Augustine allows that those who unite for incontinence alone but keep faith and do not prevent offspring may be called married.
claims: Spouses may separate bodily but not sacramentally while they live.
The marriage bond remains despite adultery or separation.
The sacrament good signifies the union of Christ and the Church.
Faith and offspring may be lacking without annulling marriage; the sacrament may not.
The good of offspring is the desire to raise children religiously.
